random.title: Wild Animal Ethics
random.extract:
Wild Animal Ethics: The Moral and Political Problem of Wild Animal Suffering is a 2020 book by philosopher Kyle Johannsen, published by Routledge. It examines the moral and political obligations humans may have to reduce wild animal suffering, including suffering caused by natural processes rather than human activities. Drawing on deontological ethics and political philosophy, Johannsen argues that humans have a collective obligation to assist wild animals and to research safe methods of reducing suffering on a large scale.
The book discusses predation, disease, starvation, adverse weather, injury and parasitism, as well as reproductive strategies that result in high juvenile mortality. Johannsen examines objections to intervention based on the value of nature, animal liberty and ecological risks. He considers genetic engineering, including CRISPR and gene drives, as possible means of reducing suffering without requiring continuous human management of wild animal populations.
The book was discussed at an academic symposium organised by Animals in Philosophy, Politics, Law, and Ethics (APPLE) at Queen's University in 2021. Commentaries by Clare Palmer, Bob Fischer, Nicolas Delon and Gary David O'Brien, together with Johannsen's response, were subsequently published in Philosophia.

entry.title: The Moon Watchers
entry.summary:
Explanation: On November 24, all denizens of our fair planet could watch the Moon rise opposite the setting Sun. Easy to spot in twilight skies above fields, fences, backyards, and even stone walls, the Moon was big and bright, and at its full phase. Known to some as a Beaver Moon, November's Full Moon was also near perigee, the closest point in its elliptical orbit around planet Earth. That made it one of the biggest and brightest Full Moons, also known as a supermoon. In fact, November's Full Moon was the first in a series of four consecutive Full Moons near perigee. So your next chance to watch a supermoon rise will be when the Cold Moon rises on December 23.
